ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZh2qAA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDIwC4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 61, "title": "Correct ordinary V30MZ IN/OUT timing without double-counting transfers", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `7f4e1871edb1153bc4df4b4af8cc377c5ff36ddc`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:640–660` leaves E4–E7/EC–EF on the default one-clock execution component. With no-wait RAM fetches and byte or eligible aligned-word I/O, current totals are three clocks for DX forms and four for immediate forms. These are static deductions, not planning-time executions.

Understated I/O time changes register polling and CPU progress relative to raster events, timers, audio and DMA. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

Correct all eight ordinary byte/word IN/OUT encodings while retaining the existing explicit fetch approximation and transfer classification. Reconcile the documented decoded interval with already charged I/O transfers, rather than adding six clocks to every existing charge.

For the retained scheduling policy, use `total = fetch_charges + 6 + (I/O_transfer_charges − 1)`. No-wait RAM byte/eligible-even-word totals consequently become seven clocks for DX and eight for immediate forms; split-word totals become eight/nine. These totals describe the emulator's bounded policy, not complete silicon pipeline timing.

## Context

The clean checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. Open Issues/PRs are empty; all 60 closed-work titles contain no equivalent completed correction. [Issue #39](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/39) corrected transfer accounting and explicitly deferred absolute instruction timing. Preserve its bus-width, lane and alignment acceptance.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), Appendix A, specifies six clocks for ordinary immediate/DX IN/OUT after decoding, under its no-wait/even-word conditions. Chapter 4 establishes transfer costs. The formula above is an explicit integration inference: its normal data transfer is already included, while this emulator separately charges instruction fetches. Full prefetch and intra-instruction device ordering remain outside this task.

Correction record: replace the AI-authored assumption that the existing one-clock execution component and three/four-clock assertions demonstrate ordinary I/O accuracy. Apply the documented decoded interval without charging its normal transfer twice. Record old assumption, corrected requirement, source and rationale; evidence-backed technical corrections require no human approval or independent AI re-review.

[WSTimingTest's report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSTimingTest/blob/025e606fc3b6615160ffdae485d992ffcad0c024/README.md), opcode cases and harness were inspected. Its measured loop expectations include prefetch, branches and glue instructions, so they are not individual-instruction totals or acceptance constants.

Existing unit assertions and native/browser word-timing probes are present; the probes primarily compare relative alignment costs. [Saved #59 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/7f4e1871edb1153bc4df4b4af8cc377c5ff36ddc/docs/issue-59-validation.md) reports 164 core unit tests, 30 integration tests, one adapter test and complete production Chromium suites passing. Those saved results were not rerun here and do not establish corrected I/O timing. Its final Coordinator review remains requested in the inspected records.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the reconciled timing table before implementation. Cover all eight encodings, internal byte/eligible-even-word/split-word transfers, cartridge byte-wide I/O and existing applicable waits. Assert the literal seven/eight and eight/nine RAM totals above; retain actual ROM fetch/wait charges and charge each additional transfer/wait once. Preserve raw bus accounting for other instructions and DMA.
- [ ] Correct ordinary decoding and add independent literal timing/data vectors. Check instruction length, continuation, AL-versus-AX effects, unchanged FLAGS/unrelated state, byte-lane masks and side effects. Preserve prefix/BUSLOCK behavior, existing REP rejection, port-wrap/error behavior and INS/OUTS semantics. Update obsolete total-clock expectations without weakening transfer-width or relative-alignment assertions.
- [ ] Cover all nine supported static emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations and Color/Crystal runtime round trips `00→80→00→C0→00→E0→00`. Exercise RAM and mapped-ROM instruction fetches, live ROM controls, valid odd internal ports and cartridge I/O waits where available. Resolve any newly discovered timing requirement from primary evidence rather than fitting observed output.
- [ ] Through normal Machine scheduling, demonstrate corrected elapsed clocks advance timers, raster/frame state and PCM exactly once. Cover an I/O burst crossing a line/frame boundary and existing separate GDMA/SDMA accounting; preserve interrupt delivery and HALT continuation.
- [ ] Add or extend an original source-included CC0 timing cartridge using the existing NASM/`fixtures/build.py` pipeline. Native and production Chromium/Wasm checks must compare CPU-written elapsed-time observations against independently calculated expectations for immediate/DX byte/word bursts, with explicit timer quantization bounds. Cover all three models, supported runtime mode transitions and fresh restart; clear volatile results and invalidate retained success. Record focused unit/native-cartridge baseline failures and corrected passes. Preserve the existing relative word-timing probe.
- [ ] Coordinator passes and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, pass `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against local production preview. Identify the final functional revision each result covers.
- [ ] Preserve prior CPU/interrupt, three-model startup/firmware, video/input/frame, audio/PCM, DMA/Hyper Voice, RTC transport, SRAM/EEPROM and Wasm/browser lifecycle/save-integrity behavior. Preserve raw ROM identity, ownership/provenance and browser-local handling. Document timing limits and actual failures, resolutions, passes and unperformed checks. Coordinator reviews every criterion and resolves blocking findings before merge.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-browser discrimination, additional lawful software experiments or another browser engine. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are optional and were unperformed during planning. No files changed, remote content was published, agents were spawned, or application builds/tests were executed.

## Required post-merge verification

None

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
